Mabon is readying his memory snares. Collect refined essence of magic throughout the air to power them on.

Isgarren, 

Couldn't find you this morning for a chat, so I left this brief of what I wanted to discuss in your robe pocket. Waiting Dawn mentioned you were accompanying the wayfinder to more tropical surrounds. She was glad to have a chance to spend time in Amnytas, after all this time. I wanted to get her to jot down some notes on the Heart of the Obscure while she's here, but Dagda asked I not disturb her while she communes with the World Spire. 

Once again, trying to extract straightforward answers from you elder wizards is like trying to pry a diamond from a skritt's hands. 

Meanwhile, the Tyrian Alliance continues to drag their heels on our proposal to further assess activity in the Realm of Torment after Kormir's exodus and other recent events. My own digging during the titan mess turned up nothing new. Lucky for us, your expedition into Bava Nisos gave you a chance to assess the foundry, albeit from a distance. Maybe one day the alliance council will see the benefit of a more thorough investigation. 

For now, I've been fielding the occasional request from Ogden Stonehealer since our talks with the priory began. He and some of the other Deldrimor would like to talk, and I'm of two minds about it—figuratively speaking. You know my facets had some nasty bouts with Kryptis possession while you were wrestling with Cerus. Some of my suppressed memories were dredged to the surface, and well, let's just say my chances of a family reunion are pretty damn slim. Still, with dwarven memories being what they are, who can say if someone's kept a lantern lit for me, you know? 

Enough about my own baggage. Enjoy yourself! Let some of the world's weight off those world-bearing shoulders. 

Safe travels,  
Lyhr

I've always wanted to leave this place. Kaineng. It was sad to leave the shop behind, but I can open a shop anywhere. Elona, even. I'd like to see other places besides Cantha... I've barely even left the city.

We found an abandoned vault in the Undercity—I think it belonged to the royal family. Not a lot left in here, aside from a few locked chests and some old tapestries. Dalnim found a necromancer that was willing to seal the door. He owed her a favor, big surprise. It'll only open for us so it's safe inside. She has some loose ends to tie up before we can leave, but I'll hide out in here until we're ready to go.

Somewhere without the Jade Brotherhood or Am Fah... No ministries to tell us what to do. Just us, Dalnim and me. Hey, maybe we'll get a cat!

strings.en:
*(A handwritten note sits atop a small pile of maps, charts, and documents.)*  

  
Captain Sayida,  

  
These materials were all I could dig up from our humble maritime archive in the city. Pretty sure some of them were on loan from the Priory and I never got around to returning them.  
  
The earliest mentions of Castora appear in ancient Margonite sailing records before the fall, when their ships ruled the Unending Ocean. Others come from ancient Canthan vessels, rumored to have been blessed or guided by celestial entities. A good number of these records were supposedly plundered by corsair fleets between 324 AE and the end of the First Great Corsair War around 712 AE. After that, they traded hands between corsairs and other pirates before the raising of Orr.  
  
Descriptions are few. There is consistent mention of an unusual marine layer that blankets the entire coast of the island continent. For the most part, they read as if they were mostly written from the ships, stopping to fish or scrounge for wreck salvage, only to catch the briefest silhouette or outline of a landmass.  
  
That's all that stood out from a skim; perhaps you'll have better luck. Based on your reputation, if anyone has a half a shot of reaching the shore, it's a Sly. With that said, I'm looking forward to hearing what Castora has to offer Lion's Arch, Captain.  

   
Safe seas,  
Commadore Lawson Marriner

(This old letter is thin and fragile, having no doubt been read many hundreds of times.)

My dearest Isgarren,

I have left this letter with Waiting Sorrow, and I ask you not to be angry with her if she delivers it to you. She has done me a kindness and deserves no blame for that.

If you're reading this, my love, then I am gone. Do not blame yourself for this; I have known, at every moment, the danger that we must face. And I have known also the reasons why those risks are worth it. I've never regretted my choice even once. I would choose this path again without hesitation.

But I must confess something to you: While each of us has always been sworn to protect this world, it has always been my true duty to protect you. Because your shoulders, my love, are too broad to ever go without a burden, your mind too vast to ever have any peace. I hope that, in my time with you, I have eased the weight of the mantle. Even you deserve rest.

I do not fear for Tyria in my passing; Tyria, always, finds a pathway forward. I fear for you, for the responsibility that you insist must fall always on yourself. So please, do not treat Tyria as your burden alone. No one, not even you, is made to bear such a weight. Instead, trust those around you, believe in the peoples that we have shepherded, and most importantly of all, do not dwell on what might have been. No matter how the end may have come to me, I wouldn't have traded my years with you for anything.

I will wait, beyond the stars, for the day when I am with you again. And I hope, for Tyria's sake, that it is not too soon.

Yours, until the end of eternity,
Vass
